newsitem.title: GERMANY: GEA sees notable rise in 1997 profits.
newsitem.headline: GEA sees notable rise in 1997 profits.

text.p: German energy and environmental equipment group Gea AG said on Monday it expected its 1997 net profit to be notably higher after reporting solid growth in sales and incoming orders for the first half.

The company said its group sales rose to 1.891 billion marks ($1 billion) in the first six months of the year compared with 1.688 billion in the same period of 1996. Incoming orders rose to 2.467 billion marks from 2.284 billion.

The company also said its net debt fell sharply, totalling 328 million marks at June 30 down from 676 million. Gea defines its net debt as financial debts after deduction of securities holdings and liquid assets.
Gea reported net profit of 105.5 million marks for 1996.
The company said it remained interested in expanding through acquisition in the future and was waiting for a suitable opportunity to present itself.
